messages:
Maya (Elmwood): morning team — we started seeing massive tail latency for elmwood-prod around 11:20 UTC. p99 on /v1/generate shot from ~300ms -> ~4.8s. Some requests are 5xx/timeouts. We're on Reserved (pool dc-7). Example slow reqs: req_1a2b3c4d, req_1b2c3d4e. Can ops take a look?

Emma S.: thanks Maya. Can you paste tenant id + a redacted example payload and confirm pool (dc-7) + reserved/dedicated? Also any client-side retry or batch that could coincide?

Maya (Elmwood): tenant=elmwood-prod. payload (redacted): {"model":"redwood-7b-compat", "prompt":"summaries...", "max_tokens":256}. Reserved pool dc-7. No app change; we had a scheduled batch job at 11:17 that sent ~2k small requests quickly.

Randall P.: pulling runtime logs for dc-7 now. Can you paste 2-3 slow request IDs and approximate client timestamps?

Maya (Elmwood): adding req_1a2b3c4d (11:20:12), req_1b2c3d4e (11:20:31), req_1c2d3e4f (11:20:45).

Randall P.: grep shows correlated kv cache churn. Snippet: 
```
[11:20:13] pool=dc-7 tenant=elmwood-prod model=redwood-7b-compat kv_cache_miss=298 kv_cache_eviction=78 seq_len=1024
[11:20:14] pool=dc-7 tenant=orion-svc model=redwood-7b-compat kv_cache_miss=412 kv_cache_eviction=96 seq_len=2048
[11:20:15] eviction_policy=LRU total_evicted=134 reason=burst
[11:20:16] req=req_1a2b3c4d latency=4921ms cold_kv_reads=12 retries=1
```
So eviction spike aligns with the burst and slow traces have many cold_kv_reads.

Javier R.: that pattern screams noisy neighbor causing KV cache thrash. Reserved pool but shared workers can still accept bursts; last week we enabled shared-burst for dc-7 to reduce throttles — that may be the root cause.

Tomas L.: confirming: we flipped "burst_on_shared_pools=true" at 09:40 UTC yesterday to reduce throttling tickets. That will allow non-reserved tenants to spill into dc-7 under load.

Emma S.: short-term mitigations (minutes) we can attempt:
- Pin elmwood to a subset of warm workers (tenant pin)
- Temporarily increase elmwood routing priority so their requests use reserved-only workers
- Apply a soft throttle to non-reserved bursts in dc-7 or rollback the burst flag for a short window
Which one can infra do fastest?

Randall P.: I can pin. Running: 
```
infractl tenant-pin --tenant elmwood-prod --pool dc-7 --workers 3 --reason "kv-churn emergency"
```
Pin request accepted; rebalancing. Expect ~60-120s for workers to move and warm caches. Monitoring p99.

Tomas L.: applying a temporary soft throttle for non-reserved traffic in dc-7: 
```
policyctl set dc-7 non_reserved.burst_rate=180rps window=60s temp=true
```
Policy applied. Watching ingress.

Maya (Elmwood): p99 dropped to ~520ms within ~2 minutes after pin + soft throttle. Users report improvement. Thanks.

Javier R.: good sign — pin reduces cross-tenant eviction pressure. Cold_kv_reads in the slow traces should decline to near zero as the cache warms.

Alice N.: ops runbook note: when a reserved tenant sees sudden tail regressions, check pool eviction logs and seq_len diversity. Treat eviction spikes >100 in 60s as noisy-neighbor candidate and trigger pin workflow. Document commands & TTLs.

Emma S.: medium-term remediation ideas (hours->weeks):
- Add per-tenant auto-pin when kv_cache_eviction_rate > threshold (pilot)
- Expose kv_cache_hit/miss and cold_kv_reads per-tenant in Console dashboards
- Add seq_len_entropy metric per pool and alert on sudden increases
- Introduce a reservation flag "deny_shared_burst" for customers who want stricter isolation (default remain backwards-compatible)

Tomas L.: I'll open a PR to add deny_shared_burst boolean on reservation objects and wire it to the routing decision. Also adding UI checkbox in Console. For current customers we'll keep existing behavior but allow opt-out.

Randall P.: follow-up notes: 
- Tenant elmwood-prod pinned to 3 workers at 11:22:01 UTC
- Eviction counts in dc-7 fell from ~134 -> 6 over the next 90s
- p99 for elmwood from 4.9s -> 520ms at 11:24:10 UTC
- We did not rollback burst flag yet; we applied a soft throttle instead

Maya (Elmwood): can you add a temporary allowlist so our scheduled batch doesn't get throttled while pinned? We want to continue bursts but without impacting other tenants.

Emma S.: adding allowlist: 
```
policyctl add-allowlist --tenant elmwood-prod --job-pattern "elmwood-batch-*" --pool dc-7 --priority high --ttl 3h
```
Allowlist added for 3h. Monitor and report if anything unusual.

Javier R.: runtime action items for eng-runtime: 
- Implement auto-detect + auto-pin prototype (pilot)
- Improve eviction policy: consider LRUC with hotset retention and prefetching on cold hits
- Expose per-tenant cold_kv_reads and eviction_rate metrics to Console and alerts

Alice N.: ops follow-ups: update runbook with the pin workflow, sample commands, and when to escalate to eng-runtime. Add a checklist: check eviction logs, seq_len entropy, attempt pin, add allowlist if necessary.

Randall P.: extending pin TTL to 4h at request of Maya. Created infra ticket to revisit burst policy on dc-7 if repeat incidents occur.

InfraBot: Incident recorded: INC-2026-0428. Assigned: eng-runtime, eng-platform. Severity: P2. Timeline saved.

Maya (Elmwood): thanks everyone — traffic stable for 20m, p99 ~480ms. Please keep me posted on the RFC for reservation isolation and the auto-pin pilot.

Emma S.: will do. Closing immediate escalation; tracking follow-ups via INC-2026-0428 and new RFC. Thanks team :thumbsup:
